text: Now put a membrane in the way. Turn the field so the outside of the cell is at the top and the cytoplasm below, then slide in a phospholipid bilayer, with the gradient running across it. Our example is a red blood cell taking up oxygen in a lung capillary. Here we track freely dissolved oxygen, not oxygen bound to haemoglobin: it diffuses from the surrounding plasma into the cell. Oxygen molecules are small and non-polar, so they pass straight through the bilayer, hydrophobic core included, down their concentration gradient. That is simple diffusion: no transport protein needed.
